themes_detail.label: Indoor Air Quality Crisis
themes_detail.summary: Indoor air quality complaints spiked to 7 THIS WEEK versus a baseline of 1.2 per week over the prior 8 weeks—a 460% increase (z-score: 5.28)—suggesting a potential acute environmental or building health hazard affecting multiple residences in Hunts Point.
evidence: 7 indoor air quality complaints filed THIS WEEK vs. 1.2 weekly baseline (460% spike, z-score: 5.28)
Spike coincides with elevated plumbing complaints (4 THIS WEEK vs. 0.8 baseline) and general unsanitary conditions (501 complaints over 90 days), suggesting potential moisture/mold drivers
Community board has repeatedly requested additional building inspectors, indicating chronic inspection capacity gaps that may enable indoor air hazards to persist undetected
reporting_angles: Door-knock canvass of residential buildings with multiple complaints to document symptoms and identify common source (HVAC malfunction, mold, external pollution)
Interview HPD/DEP officials on whether they've investigated clusters; cross-check with Building Department permit and violation data

themes_detail.label: Curb/Street Surface Deterioration
themes_detail.summary: Curb condition complaints exploded to 3 THIS WEEK from a baseline of 0.1 per week—a 2300% spike (z-score: 8.69, highest statistical significance)—signaling rapid street infrastructure failure in the district, potentially tied to the city's recent trash bin expansion announcement.
evidence: 3 curb condition complaints THIS WEEK vs. 0.1 weekly average (2300% spike, z-score: 8.69—highest statistical severity in dataset)

amNewYork reported on April 17 that 'Two Bronx districts tapped for major NYC trash bin expansion,' including Hunts Point/Longwood, suggesting infrastructure stress preceding or accompanying new waste infrastructure
Spike appears isolated to THIS WEEK, indicating acute recent event (e.g., new bins installed, street excavation, pothole formation) rather than chronic condition
reporting_angles: Verify timeline: Did trash bin installations begin THIS WEEK? Visit reported complaint addresses to document curb damage and photograph
Interview DSNY about rollout timeline and whether they've received complaints about installation damage or bin placement blocking curbs

themes_detail.label: Graffiti Uptick
themes_detail.summary: Graffiti complaints surged to 4 THIS WEEK from a baseline of 0.8 per week—a 433% spike (z-score: 3.36)—suggesting a new or concentrated tagging campaign in the district.
evidence: 4 graffiti complaints filed THIS WEEK vs. 0.8 weekly baseline (433% spike, z-score: 3.36)
Spike is recent and acute, appearing THIS WEEK only; no prior escalation in prior 8-week baseline
Aligns with broader Bronx street disorder concerns, though isolated to CD 202
reporting_angles: Map the 4 complaint locations to determine if they cluster geographically (suggesting coordinated tagging) or are dispersed
Contact Parks/Sanitation to confirm removal timeline and whether they've identified a tagger crew

themes_detail.label: Elevator Failures in Multi-Family Housing
themes_detail.summary: Elevator complaints peaked at 22 THREE WEEKS AGO, representing a 184% spike versus the 7.8 weekly baseline (z-score: 4.0)—a lagging but significant indicator of deferred maintenance in residential buildings, compounded by the community board's ongoing pleas for more building inspectors.
evidence: 22 elevator complaints filed 3 WEEKS AGO vs. 7.8 weekly baseline (184% spike, z-score: 4.0)

Community board has submitted identical budget requests year after year to 'assign additional building inspectors,' indicating chronic understaffing prevents timely detection and enforcement of maintenance violations
Spike is lagging (not THIS WEEK), but statistical severity remains high; unclear if elevated complaints have since normalized or persist
reporting_angles: Follow up: Are elevator complaints still elevated, or did they return to baseline after 3 weeks? A sustained trend warrants deeper investigation
Interview HPD/DOB on inspector vacancy rates and average time-to-inspection for residential elevator complaints in CD 202; compare to city average

themes_detail.label: Plumbing Crisis in Aging Housing Stock
themes_detail.summary: Plumbing complaints spiked to 4 LAST WEEK (vs. 0.8 baseline, 433% increase, z-score: 4.91) amid concurrent elevated indoor air quality and water leak complaints, pointing to systemic deterioration in building water infrastructure—a leading indicator of habitability hazards.
evidence: 4 plumbing complaints LAST WEEK vs. 0.8 weekly baseline (433% spike, z-score: 4.91)
Water leak complaints: 194 over 90 days (substantial baseline), suggesting chronic undersized or deteriorated water systems

Convergence signal: elevated plumbing + elevated indoor air quality complaints THIS WEEK + 501 unsanitary condition complaints over 90 days suggest interconnected building health failures (mold from leaks, poor ventilation from blocked vents)
Heat/hot water complaints dominate 90-day data at 2,311, indicating systemic building system failures across multiple systems
reporting_angles: Obtain HPD violations data for CD 202: How many buildings have open Class B (hazardous) or Class C (non-hazardous) violations for water leaks, mold, or heating in the past 12 months?
Interview tenants in buildings with multiple plumbing complaints about repair timelines and landlord responsiveness; investigate whether complaints cluster in specific buildings or are dispersed
